newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's Prime Minister proposes cabinet changes.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's Prime Minister proposes cabinet changes.

text.p: Vietnam's Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has proposed dropping more than 10 ministers and senior officials from his cabinet as part of a sweeping reshuffle, an informed government source said on Wednesday.
The source said delegates to the National Assembly had been presented with a list of people to be replaced, and would vote on this and a list of nominees for the vacant positions later on Wednesday.
Among those being dropped are Vietnam's Finance Minister Ho Te, Minister for Planning and Investment Do Quoc Sam, and head of the powerful Interior (police) Ministry Bui Thien Ngo, the source said.
Also included on the list are Culture and Information Minister Tran Hoan, Le Xuan Trinh of the Government Office and Nguyen Ky Cam, head of the Committee for Anti-Corruption and Smuggling.
Under Vietnam's political system their successors are unlikely to be formally appointed before the current session of the National Assembly draws to a close in about a week.
Vietnam's cabinet comprises more than 30 people, including ministers, heads of state commissions and other government bodies.
The reshuffle is set to be the first major personnel shake-up in Vietnam since a landmark Communist Party Congress in late June.
National Assembly Chairman Nong Duc Manh said last month that the changes would see older ministers stand aside for younger blood.
At last year's autumn National Assembly session Vietnam overhauled the government structure with the merging of eight departments into three super-ministries.
However, Manh said this year's changes would be personnel only and would not affect ministries, the Prime Minister or the three deputy prime ministers.
